oneLiner: The custom-ASIC arms dealer: $73B AI backlog, FY2026 AI revenue guided to ~$56B (+180%), FY2027 target above $100B, with VMware cash flows funding the ride.
thesis: Only vendor combining leading-edge XPU co-design (serdes, packaging, 2nm roadmap) with the Ethernet AI-networking franchise (Tomahawk): the default partner for hyperscaler silicon.

Disclosed/reported custom-ASIC customers: Google (TPU, 7 generations), Meta (MTIA), OpenAI (10GW deal, first deployments H2 2026), Anthropic (1GW scaling to 3GW), with Apple and ByteDance reported among unnamed customers.
Custom ASICs outgrowing merchant GPUs in 2026 (TrendForce: +45% vs +16%); Broadcom holds ~55-60% of the co-design market.
Infrastructure software (VMware, ~32% of revenue) throws off sticky high-margin cash: 77% gross margin, 46% FCF margin company-wide.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 FY2026 (ended May 3, 2026; reported Jun 3, 2026)
points: AI semiconductor revenue $10.8B, +143% YoY (networking ~40% of it).
Non-GAAP gross margin 77.1%; record ~67% operating margin; EPS $2.44; FCF $10.3B (46% of revenue).
Guide: Q3 revenue ~$29.4B with AI semis ~$16B (below ~$17.2B consensus; stock fell ~12%).
FY2026 AI revenue raised to ~$56B (+180%); FY2027 '>$100B' reiterated; $73B AI backlog.

segments: Semiconductor solutions ~68%: custom AI accelerators/XPUs, Tomahawk AI networking, wireless, broadband, storage.
Infrastructure software ~32%: VMware, mainframe, security. AI run-rate exiting FY2026 near ~$50B annualized.
competitive: NVDA merchant silicon is the pricing umbrella; ASIC adoption erodes its share at the margin.
Marvell (~15% of custom co-design) architects Trainium and Maia; Apr 2026 reports of Google-Marvell talks on inference chips show sockets are contestable.
VMware alternatives (Nutanix, Proxmox, hyperscaler-native) gaining pilot interest amid the pricing revolt; EU investigation underway.
moat: Multi-year, multi-gigawatt co-design contracts and a $73B AI backlog institutionalize the hyperscaler relationships; serdes/packaging IP plus Ethernet networking is a package no rival matches. VMware's installed base sustains pricing power despite the backlash.
risks: Expectation risk: the >$100B FY2027 target leaves no room for slippage; a $1.2B guide miss cost 12% in a day.
Customer concentration: a handful of hyperscalers drive AI revenue; multi-sourcing (Google-Marvell) is live.
Margin mix: management flagged pressure from lower-margin custom accelerators.
VMware backlash: renewals at ~5x prior cost documented, AT&T suit, EU probe; software only +9% YoY.
OpenAI/Anthropic gigawatt commitments depend on their funding and power buildout timelines.
catalysts: Q3 FY2026 earnings Sept 2, 2026: the $16B AI quarter and FY27 reaffirmation.
New unnamed XPU customer disclosures; next-gen Tomahawk ramps.
December Q4 report as first read on the FY27 $100B trajectory.
pricedIn: ~$415 is ~16% below the high; ~65x trailing, ~22-26x forward. No longer priced for perfection but still elevated vs pre-VMware history. Debate: is the $73B backlog and $100B FY27 guide bankable (making ~22x cheap for 40-60% growth), or do concentration, Marvell encroachment, and accelerator margin dilution cap the multiple?

scenarios.bear: AI guidance misses compound: a hyperscaler dual-sources, OpenAI slips past H2 2026, accelerator mix drags margins, EU forces VMware concessions; FY27 lands well under $100B and the stock revisits the low-$300s/high-$200s.
scenarios.base: FY2026 AI lands ~$56B, FY27 tracks to roughly $100B on Google/Meta/OpenAI/Anthropic ramps; software grinds high-single-digit; EPS compounds 30%+; stock grinds toward the high-$400s as quarters de-risk the backlog.
scenarios.bull: FY27 AI exceeds $100B with new customers confirmed; Ethernet scale-up wins expand networking share; VMware stabilizes; re-rates on ~$50B+ annual FCF as the second pillar of AI silicon.

valPresets.note: FCF is compounding fast (Q2 FY26 FCF $10.3B vs $36.5B TTM); base preset (35% year-1, fading) tracks the >$100B FY27 AI revenue path.
